metadata.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
metadata.authors: Kaiming He, Xiangyu Zhang, Shaoqing Ren, Jian Sun

nodes.name: Degradation problem in deep networks
nodes.statement: When network depth increases, training accuracy gets saturated and then degrades rapidly; adding more layers to a suitably deep model leads to higher training error, and this degradation is not caused by overfitting.
nodes.statement_latex: When network depth increases, accuracy gets saturated and then degrades rapidly; adding more layers to a suitably deep model leads to higher training error, and this degradation is not caused by overfitting.

nodes.name: Vanishing/exploding gradients
nodes.statement: The notorious problem of vanishing/exploding gradients hampers convergence of deep networks from the beginning; largely addressed by normalized initialization and intermediate normalization layers (BN).

nodes.name: ImageNet classification (1000 classes)
nodes.statement: Classify images from the ImageNet 2012 dataset (1000 classes), measured by top-1 and top-5 error on 50k validation and 100k test images.

nodes.name: CIFAR-10 classification
nodes.statement: Classify $32 \times 32$ images into 10 classes from the CIFAR-10 dataset (50k training, 10k test images).

nodes.name: Object detection on PASCAL VOC and MS COCO
nodes.statement: Detect and localize objects in images from PASCAL VOC 2007/2012 and MS COCO datasets, measured by mAP.

nodes.name: ImageNet localization (LOC)
nodes.statement: Classify and localize the dominant object in an ImageNet image, evaluated by top-5 localization error.

nodes.name: Underlying mapping $\mathcal{H}(\mathbf{x})$
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{H}(\mathbf{x})$ is the underlying mapping to be fit by a few stacked nonlinear layers, with $\mathbf{x}$ the input to the first of these layers.

nodes.name: Residual function $\mathcal{F}(\mathbf{x})$
nodes.statement: Given desired underlying mapping $\mathcal{H}(\mathbf{x})$, the residual function is $\mathcal{F}(\mathbf{x}) := \mathcal{H}(\mathbf{x}) - \mathbf{x}$, so that the original mapping becomes $\mathcal{F}(\mathbf{x}) + \mathbf{x}$.

nodes.name: Residual building block (identity shortcut)
nodes.statement: $\mathbf{y} = \mathcal{F}(\mathbf{x}, \{W_i\}) + \mathbf{x}$, where $\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}$ are input/output vectors and $\mathcal{F}$ is the residual mapping (e.g. $\mathcal{F} = W_2 \sigma(W_1 \mathbf{x})$ with $\sigma$ ReLU).

nodes.name: Projection shortcut
nodes.statement: When dimensions of $\mathbf{x}$ and $\mathcal{F}$ differ, a linear projection $W_s$ is applied: $\mathbf{y} = \mathcal{F}(\mathbf{x}, \{W_i\}) + W_s \mathbf{x}$.

nodes.name: Bottleneck building block
nodes.statement: A 3-layer residual block with $1\times 1$, $3\times 3$, $1\times 1$ convolutions; the $1\times 1$ layers reduce then restore dimensions, leaving the $3\times 3$ layer a bottleneck.

nodes.name: Plain network (VGG-style baseline)
nodes.statement: A baseline CNN inspired by VGG: convolutional layers with mostly $3\times 3$ filters following two rules: same #filters for same output map size, and #filters doubled when feature map size is halved; ends with global average pooling and a 1000-way FC + softmax.

nodes.name: Residual network (ResNet)
nodes.statement: The plain network with shortcut connections inserted across each pair of $3\times 3$ filters, turning it into its residual counterpart; identity shortcuts are used when input/output dimensions match, projection shortcuts otherwise.

nodes.name: Shortcut option A (zero-padding)
nodes.statement: When dimensions increase, the shortcut performs identity mapping with extra zero entries padded for the new channels; introduces no extra parameter.

nodes.name: Shortcut option B (projection on dim-increase)
nodes.statement: Identity shortcuts when dimensions match; $1\times 1$ projection shortcuts (Eqn.\ref{eq:transform}) used only when dimensions increase.

nodes.name: Shortcut option C (all projections)
nodes.statement: All shortcuts are $1\times 1$ projection shortcuts $W_s \mathbf{x}$, regardless of whether dimensions change.

nodes.name: Identity-shortcut block equation
nodes.statement: $\mathbf{y} = \mathcal{F}(\mathbf{x}, \{W_i\}) + \mathbf{x}$

nodes.name: Projection-shortcut block equation
nodes.statement: $\mathbf{y} = \mathcal{F}(\mathbf{x}, \{W_i\}) + W_s \mathbf{x}$

nodes.name: ResNet training procedure (ImageNet)
nodes.statement: End-to-end SGD training of plain/residual networks on ImageNet with batch normalization, He initialization, and a stepwise learning rate schedule.
input: Training images resized so shorter side $\in [256, 480]$, $224\times 224$ random crops with horizontal flip and per-pixel mean subtraction
output: Trained CNN classifier evaluated by top-1 / top-5 error on ImageNet validation/test
nodes.pseudocode: Initialize weights as in He 2015. Apply BN after each convolution and before activation. Use SGD with mini-batch 256, momentum 0.9, weight decay 1e-4, no dropout. Learning rate starts at 0.1; divide by 10 when error plateaus; train for up to $60\times 10^4$ iterations. At test time use 10-crop testing, or fully-convolutional multi-scale with shorter sides $\{224,256,384,480,640\}$.

nodes.name: ResNet training procedure (CIFAR-10)
nodes.statement: Training of $6n+2$-layer plain/residual nets on CIFAR-10 with identity shortcuts (option A) and a stepwise learning rate schedule.
input: $32 \times 32$ images with per-pixel mean subtracted; 4-pixel padding plus random $32\times 32$ crop and horizontal flip
Number of stacked layers $n \in \{3,5,7,9,18,200\}$ giving 20/32/44/56/110/1202-layer nets
output: Trained classifier evaluated by error on the 10k CIFAR-10 test set
nodes.pseudocode: Initial learning rate 0.1, divided by 10 at 32k and 48k iterations; terminate at 64k iterations; weight decay 1e-4, momentum 0.9, mini-batch 128 on 2 GPUs; BN, no dropout, He initialization. For $n=18$ (110-layer): warm up with lr 0.01 until training error $<80\%$ ($\sim$400 iters), then switch to 0.1.

nodes.name: Faster R-CNN with ResNet-101 (object detection)
nodes.statement: Faster R-CNN detection system with the VGG-16 backbone replaced by ResNet-101, using shared conv1--conv4_x feature maps for RPN and Fast R-CNN, and conv5_x as per-region head.
input: Detection training data (PASCAL VOC 07+12 / 07++12, MS COCO)
output: Detected bounding boxes with class labels; mAP on VOC/COCO test sets
nodes.pseudocode: Compute shared conv feature maps using layers with stride $\le 16$ (conv1, conv2_x, conv3_x, conv4_x; total 91 conv layers). Share these between an RPN (300 proposals) and Fast R-CNN. RoI pooling before conv5_1; conv5_x and above act as per-region head. Replace final classification with two sibling layers (cls and box reg). After pre-training, fix BN statistics during fine-tuning.

nodes.name: Per-class RPN localization with R-CNN refinement
nodes.statement: Localization algorithm using a per-class RPN (1000-d binary cls layer + $1000\times 4$-d reg layer) on ResNet-101, with R-CNN re-scoring of top proposals.
input: $224\times 224$ random crops; mini-batch 256; 8 anchors per image at 1:1 pos/neg ratio
output: Bounding boxes per class; top-5 localization error on ImageNet validation/test
nodes.pseudocode: Per-class RPN with two sibling $1\times 1$ conv layers (cls and reg). Train on per-class anchors. Apply RPN to predict GT-class boxes and use the top-200 as class-dependent proposals to fine-tune an R-CNN classifier (RoI-centric, mini-batch 256). At test time, RPN generates top-200 proposals per predicted class; R-CNN updates scores and box positions.

nodes.name: Faster R-CNN baseline
nodes.statement: Two-stage detector combining a region proposal network and a Fast R-CNN detection head with shared conv features.

nodes.name: Batch Normalization
nodes.statement: Layer that normalizes activations to zero mean / unit variance per mini-batch, then applies learnable scale/shift; placed after each convolution and before activation.

nodes.name: He initialization
nodes.statement: Variance-scaling weight initialization tailored for ReLU networks; used to start plain/residual nets from scratch.

nodes.name: VGG network (baseline architecture)
nodes.statement: Very deep CNN with $3\times 3$ convolutions, used as the design philosophy basis for the plain baseline; VGG-19 has 19.6 billion FLOPs.

nodes.name: Highway networks
nodes.statement: Networks with shortcut connections gated by data-dependent gating functions with parameters; when a gate is closed, layers represent non-residual functions.

nodes.name: Constructed-solution argument for non-degradation
nodes.statement: There exists by construction a deeper model with training error no greater than its shallower counterpart: copy the shallower layers and set added layers to identity. Hence current solvers, not capacity, cause the degradation problem.
assumptions: A shallower model has been trained to a given training error
Added layers can be configured as identity mappings
conclusions: The deeper model should produce no higher training error than its shallower counterpart

nodes.name: Residual reformulation eases optimization near identity
nodes.statement: If the optimal function is closer to an identity mapping than to a zero mapping, it is easier for the solver to find perturbations relative to identity than to learn the function as new; in the limit, if the identity is optimal, pushing residuals to zero is easier than fitting an identity by stacked nonlinear layers.
assumptions: The optimal function is closer to identity than to zero
conclusions: Solver can find optimum more easily than for the unreferenced formulation

nodes.name: Identity shortcuts add no parameters or computation
nodes.statement: The identity shortcut $\mathbf{y} = \mathcal{F}(\mathbf{x}, \{W_i\}) + \mathbf{x}$ introduces neither extra parameter nor computational complexity (beyond a negligible element-wise addition), enabling fair comparison between plain and residual networks of equal depth, width, and FLOPs.
conclusions: No additional parameters or FLOPs are added by the shortcut
Plain vs. residual nets can be compared with identical capacity

nodes.name: Bottleneck identity shortcut saves complexity
nodes.statement: Replacing the identity shortcut in a bottleneck block with a projection doubles the time complexity and model size, since the shortcut connects to the two high-dimensional ends.
conclusions: Identity shortcuts lead to more efficient bottleneck designs

nodes.name: 20- vs 56-layer plain CIFAR-10 (degradation teaser)
nodes.statement: On CIFAR-10, a 56-layer plain network has higher training and test error than a 20-layer plain network, illustrating the degradation problem.

nodes.name: Plain-18 vs plain-34 on ImageNet
nodes.statement: 34-layer plain net has top-1 error 28.54% vs 27.94% for the 18-layer plain net on ImageNet validation (10-crop), confirming the degradation problem on ImageNet.

nodes.name: ResNet-18 vs ResNet-34 on ImageNet
nodes.statement: ResNet-34 (25.03%) is 2.85% better than ResNet-18 (27.88%) and 3.5% better than plain-34 (28.54%) in top-1 error on ImageNet, showing residual learning resolves the degradation problem and gains accuracy from depth.

nodes.name: Identity vs projection shortcuts (A/B/C)
nodes.statement: On ResNet-34: option A (zero-padding) 25.03%, option B (projection on dim-increase) 24.52%, option C (all projections) 24.19% top-1 error; differences are small, so projection shortcuts are not essential for resolving degradation.

nodes.name: Deeper bottleneck ResNets on ImageNet
nodes.statement: ResNet-50 (20.74/5.25%), ResNet-101 (19.87/4.60%), ResNet-152 (19.38/4.49%) single-model top-1/top-5 errors on ImageNet validation; the 152-layer ResNet has lower complexity (11.3 GFLOPs) than VGG-16/19 (15.3/19.6 GFLOPs).

nodes.name: ILSVRC 2015 classification ensemble (3.57%)
nodes.statement: An ensemble of six ResNets (with two 152-layer at submission) achieves 3.57% top-5 error on the ImageNet test set, winning 1st place at ILSVRC 2015 classification.

nodes.name: CIFAR-10 ResNet-110 (6.43%)
nodes.statement: ResNet-110 (1.7M params) achieves 6.43% (best) / 6.61$\pm$0.16% (mean) test error on CIFAR-10, comparable to state-of-the-art with fewer parameters than FitNet/Highway.

nodes.name: 1202-layer CIFAR ResNet
nodes.statement: A 1202-layer ResNet ($n=200$) trains with no optimization difficulty (training error $<0.1\%$) and achieves 7.93% test error, worse than ResNet-110 due to overfitting on this small dataset.

nodes.name: Layer response std analysis
nodes.statement: Standard deviations of CIFAR layer responses show ResNets have generally smaller responses than plain counterparts, and deeper ResNets have smaller magnitudes — supporting that residual functions are closer to zero.

nodes.name: PASCAL VOC / COCO baseline detection
nodes.statement: Replacing VGG-16 with ResNet-101 in baseline Faster R-CNN: VOC07 73.2$\to$76.4 mAP, VOC12 70.4$\to$73.8 mAP; COCO mAP@.5 41.5$\to$48.4, mAP@[.5,.95] 21.2$\to$27.2 (a 28% relative improvement).

nodes.name: COCO detection improvements + ensemble
nodes.statement: On COCO: baseline ResNet-101 48.4/27.2 mAP, +box refinement 49.9/29.9, +context 51.1/30.0, +multi-scale testing 53.8/32.5 (val); ensemble of 3 nets achieves 59.0/37.4 on test-dev, winning 1st place at COCO 2015 detection.

nodes.name: ImageNet detection (DET) result
nodes.statement: Single ResNet-101 model achieves 58.8% mAP on ImageNet DET test; ensemble of 3 models achieves 62.1% mAP, winning 1st place at ILSVRC 2015 detection (8.5 absolute points over 2nd place).

nodes.name: ImageNet localization (9.0%)
nodes.statement: Per-class RPN with ResNet-101 achieves 11.7% LOC error on GT classes; RPN+RCNN reaches 10.6% top-5 LOC error (single model) and 8.9/9.0% (ensemble) on val/test, winning 1st place at ILSVRC 2015 localization (64% relative reduction vs ILSVRC 14).

nodes.name: Optimization difficulty not from vanishing gradients
nodes.statement: Plain nets trained with BN have non-zero forward variances and healthy backward gradient norms, so the degradation is unlikely caused by vanishing gradients; the authors conjecture exponentially low convergence rates.

nodes.name: $W_s$ used only when matching dimensions
nodes.statement: A square $W_s$ in the identity equation is permissible, but experiments show identity mapping is sufficient and economical for addressing degradation; $W_s$ is therefore used only when dimensions must be matched.

nodes.name: Residual learning principle is generic
nodes.statement: The strong evidence on classification, detection, localization, and segmentation suggests the residual learning principle is generic and applicable in other vision and non-vision problems.

nodes.name: Reason for plain-net optimization difficulty
nodes.statement: Why deep plain networks exhibit exponentially low convergence rates / degradation despite BN and healthy gradients is left for future study.

nodes.name: Universal approximation of residuals
nodes.statement: Whether multiple nonlinear layers can asymptotically approximate complicated functions remains an open question (cited Montufar 2014).

nodes.name: Regularization for very deep ResNets
nodes.statement: Combining residual networks with stronger regularization (maxout/dropout) to overcome overfitting on small datasets like CIFAR-10 is left for future work.

nodes.name: Data preprocessing and augmentation
nodes.statement: Resize image so the shorter side is sampled in $[256, 480]$; randomly crop $224\times 224$ from the image or its horizontal flip; subtract per-pixel mean; apply standard color augmentation.

nodes.name: Initialize weights and BN
nodes.statement: Initialize weights as in He 2015 and insert BN after each convolution and before activation; train all plain/residual nets from scratch.

nodes.name: SGD training loop
nodes.statement: Run SGD with mini-batch 256, momentum 0.9, weight decay $10^{-4}$, no dropout; learning rate 0.1, divided by 10 when error plateaus; train up to $60\times 10^4$ iterations.

nodes.name: Test-time evaluation
nodes.statement: For comparison, use 10-crop testing (Krizhevsky 2012); for best results, fully-convolutional multi-scale evaluation with shorter sides $\in \{224,256,384,480,640\}$, averaging scores.

nodes.name: CIFAR data preparation and augmentation
nodes.statement: Per-pixel mean subtracted from $32\times 32$ inputs; pad 4 pixels on each side and randomly crop $32\times 32$ from the padded image or horizontal flip.

nodes.name: CIFAR SGD with stepwise schedule
nodes.statement: Train with mini-batch 128 on 2 GPUs; lr starts at 0.1, divided by 10 at 32k and 48k iterations; terminate at 64k iterations; weight decay $10^{-4}$, momentum 0.9, BN, no dropout.

nodes.name: Warm-up for 110-layer ResNet
nodes.statement: If $n=18$ (110-layer): start with lr 0.01 until training error $<80\%$ ($\sim 400$ iterations), then switch back to 0.1 and continue with the standard schedule.

nodes.name: Compute shared conv feature maps
nodes.statement: Use ResNet-101 layers with stride $\le 16$ (conv1, conv2_x, conv3_x, conv4_x; total 91 conv layers) to compute full-image conv feature maps shared between RPN and Fast R-CNN.

nodes.name: RPN proposal generation
nodes.statement: Run an RPN on the shared feature maps to generate 300 region proposals.

nodes.name: RoI pooling and per-region head
nodes.statement: Apply RoI pooling before conv5_1; use conv5_x and above as the per-region head; replace the final classifier with two sibling layers for classification and box regression.

nodes.name: Fix BN during fine-tuning
nodes.statement: After ImageNet pre-training, compute BN means/variances on ImageNet and freeze them during detection fine-tuning, turning BN into linear activations with constant offset/scale to reduce memory.

nodes.name: Pre-train ResNet for ImageNet classification
nodes.statement: Pre-train ResNet-101 on ImageNet 1000-class classification; then fine-tune for localization with $224\times 224$ random crops and mini-batch size 256.

nodes.name: Train per-class RPN
nodes.statement: Per-class RPN ends with two sibling $1\times 1$ conv layers: a 1000-d cls (binary logistic regression per class) and a $1000\times 4$-d reg layer (per-class box regressors). 8 anchors sampled per image at 1:1 pos/neg ratio.

nodes.name: Generate per-class proposals and train R-CNN
nodes.statement: Apply per-class RPN to predict GT-class boxes on training images; use top-200 per image as class-dependent proposals to train an R-CNN classifier (mini-batch 256, RoI-centric).

nodes.name: Test-time RPN+R-CNN scoring
nodes.statement: At test time, RPN generates top-200 proposals per predicted class; R-CNN updates these proposals' scores and box positions to produce final localization output.
